display.name: GitHub
display.blurb: Read code, open pull requests and issues, and drive GitHub Actions (workflow runs, artifacts, secrets, variables) — scoped to a per-session GitHub App installation token whose permissions are minted from the granted powers.

token.hint: Create a fine-grained personal access token under GitHub Settings → Developer settings, with the permissions you want sessions to hold.

operations.comment: REST-parity asset (the gh regression): a GraphQL response echoes only the client's selection set, and `gh pr create` selects just `pullRequest { id url }` — so every field is response-first with a fallback: title/branches fall back to the mutation's request variables ($.vars, required CreatePullRequestInput fields; absent when a client inlines its arguments) and repo/number fall back to the returned PR URL.

REST-parity asset: `gh issue create` selects only `issue { id url }`, so the title falls back to the request variables and the number to the returned issue URL (both response-first for clients that select them).

GraphQL reads enter through a handful of root Query fields with the resource nested inside, so query-side gating is coarse by GitHub's schema shape — the minted token's read permissions are the real scoper (ADR 0059). `viewer`/`rateLimit` are gated under every read power because `gh` adds them incidentally to most queries; a single uncovered top-level field denies the whole request.

`gh` probes schema capabilities before commands like `gh pr checks` / `gh pr create` via aliased `__type(name: ...)` introspection queries (public schema metadata, no resource access) and hard-fails the command when the probe dies. Gate it under the same every-read-power set as `viewer`/`rateLimit`.

cli.comment: WS4: the dummy token is GITHUB_TOKEN, NOT GH_TOKEN — do not rename it back. `gh` reads both (its local auth gate passes either way), but the guest's proto build (`bufgen`) resolves its HTTPS password via `BUF_INPUT_HTTPS_PASSWORD:-GH_TOKEN:-GITHUB_PASSWORD`, so a placeholder GH_TOKEN poisoned that chain and hard-failed `pnpm build` on any proto change (campaign A4/B3). GITHUB_TOKEN is outside that chain, so GH_TOKEN stays unset and bufgen falls through to the real GITHUB_PASSWORD. The value is a harmless placeholder — the egress proxy overwrites Authorization on api.github.com with the minted token regardless (ADR 0056), so `gh` never sends this value upstream.
cli.doc:
Use `gh` to drive GitHub from this session — code, pull requests, issues, and GitHub Actions. Authentication is automatic: `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a managed placeholder the egress proxy replaces with a short-lived, capability-scoped GitHub App installation token on every request to api.github.com. The token's GitHub App permissions are MINTED from the powers your profile granted (e.g. `actions:write` → the App's `actions: write` permission), so a call your profile didn't grant fails as a 403 from GitHub, not a leak. Do NOT run `gh auth login` or set a real token.

Open a PR:
1. Re-anchor on the live base (the baked checkout may be stale): `git fetch origin && git checkout -b my-feature origin/main`.
2. Commit + push — git auth is brokered via GIT_ASKPASS, nothing to configure: `git add -A && git commit -m "..." && git push -u origin my-feature`.
3. `gh pr create --base main --title "..." --body "..."` (add `--draft` for a draft). Requires `pulls:write`. Review/merge: `gh pr review`, `gh pr merge` (pulls:write); `gh pr checks` needs `checks:read`.

Issues: `gh issue create/list/view/comment` (issues:read / issues:write). Labels & milestones ride the `issues` powers.

GitHub Actions (CI/CD):
- Runs: `gh run list`, `gh run view <id> --log`, `gh run watch <id>` need `actions:read`; `gh run rerun <id>`, `gh run cancel <id>` need `actions:write`.
- Workflows: `gh workflow list/view` (actions:read); `gh workflow run <file> -f key=val` to dispatch (actions:write).
- Artifacts & caches: list/download artifacts and `gh cache list` need `actions:read`; `gh cache delete` / deleting artifacts need `actions:write`.
- Secrets: `gh secret list` needs `secrets:read`; `gh secret set NAME` / `gh secret delete NAME` need `secrets:write` (values are write-only — GitHub never returns them).
- Variables: `gh variable list` needs `variables:read`; `gh variable set/delete` need `variables:write`.

Releases: `gh release list/view/download` (contents:read); `gh release create` / asset upload (contents:write). Repo contents, branches, commits, tags, and the Git data API ride `contents:*`; repo/metadata listings ride `metadata:read`. Commit statuses: read via `statuses:read`, set via `statuses:write`. Deployments: `deployments:read` / `deployments:write`.

Raw passthrough for anything else: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` (GET) or `gh api --method POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues -f title=...`.

GraphQL: many `gh` commands talk GraphQL (e.g. `gh pr view/list/merge/review/ready`, `gh issue view/list`, `gh repo view`) and `gh api graphql` runs it directly. These work — the egress proxy parses the GraphQL operation and gates it by the SAME power as the REST equivalent (a `mergePullRequest` mutation needs `pulls:write`, a `createIssue` mutation needs `issues:write`, read queries need a `:read` power). A GraphQL field your profile didn't grant is denied (403). Images in a PR body must be absolute URLs anchored to a commit SHA — relative repo paths do not render.
